clue.text: Be prepared for speeches and coughs

blocks.note: to be prepared for something is to expect it
formal speeches are orations

explanation.surface: A nervous speaker braces for the throat-clearing and coughing that punctuate a long round of speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Expectorations are the act of coughing up phlegm, so the plural noun stands for coughs.

clue.text: Obscure electronic excerpts on Web Central

indicators.note: the central letter is the one in the middle of the word

blocks.note: E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
clips are short excerpts from a film or broadcast
the middle letter of web

explanation.surface: Murky electronic snippets are posted on a website called Web Central.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to block it from view or outshine it, so to obscure it.

clue.text: Policeman rising at week's end, playing flute for a little change, perhaps?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom up
the end of a word is its final letter
playing with something means moving it about freely, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: cop is slang for a policeman
the last letter of week
taken as written

explanation.surface: A policeman getting up at the weekend busks on the flute for a bit of spare cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example, hence 'perhaps': coins jingling in one's pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocketful is the amount a pocket holds, and a small quantity of loose coins fits that description.

clue.text: Something soft and quiet found in copper atom

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
sh is the call for quiet
an ion is a charged atom

explanation.surface: A physicist finds a soft, silent particle inside a copper atom.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion is a soft padded object for sitting or leaning on.

clue.text: Source of one evil giant caught between alternatives

indicators.note: evil suggests something twisted and bad, so the letters are twisted out of order
a thing caught between two others is held inside them

blocks.note: either this or that: each alternative is introduced by the word or
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: The story of a wicked giant trapped between two choices, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The two ORs of the alternatives go round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An originator is the person or thing from which something starts, its creator or source.

clue.text: Each contorted in pain

indicators.note: contorted means twisted out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Everyone is twisted up in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain, so the noun matches.

clue.text: Hazard concealed by Candice Bergen…

indicators.note: something concealed by words is tucked away inside their letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the two names

explanation.surface: A danger is kept secret by the actress Candice Bergen, star of Murphy Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, most of the answer lies hidden below the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg is a large floating mass of ice and a notorious danger to shipping.

clue.text: …ot at all the first woman to appear within newspaper's covers

indicators.note: the covers of something are its outsides, its first and last letters
to appear within something is to be placed inside it

blocks.note: the outer letters of newspaper
Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a woman never once made the front page of a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The source text dropped the N of 'not' into the ellipsis: the definition reads 'not at all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Never means at no time, and as an emphatic negative it stands for not in any way.

clue.text: My note about beginning and end of trail: "Bush,…

indicators.note: only the very start and finish of the word are wanted
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
the first and last letters of trail

explanation.surface: A note quoting someone about George W. Bush, the sentence carrying on into 13 Down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the president, but it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen flowering shrub, so it is an example of a bush.

clue.text: Key person narrated "The Story of Salmon"

indicators.note: something narrated is told out loud, so the wanted word is one that is spoken the same

blocks.note: lox is cured salmon and a myth is a story

explanation.surface: Someone important reads aloud a tale about fish, like a children's audiobook.
explanation.walkthrough: Lox is the American name for smoked or cured salmon, served on bagels.
explanation.definitionFit: A locksmith makes and fits keys, so a key person in a playful, literal sense.

clue.text: Diplomat's deadly sin: hiding love

indicators.note: a thing that hides something keeps it inside itself

blocks.note: envy is one of the seven deadly sins
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A diplomat's secret vice is envy that masks real affection.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a messenger or representative sent on a diplomatic mission.

clue.text: Fort Pulaski's chief dies, or I fail

indicators.note: the chief part of a word is its head, its opening letter
a failed arrangement has broken down, so its letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: the leading letter of Pulaski
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier at a Civil War fort in Georgia fears death or failure.
explanation.walkthrough: Fort Pulaski is a real fort near Savannah, which makes 'Fort' look like part of the name rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A presidio is a fortified military post, the Spanish word used for forts in the American Southwest.

clue.text: When withdrawn, intercession shows confidence

indicators.note: the word on show lies inside the letters of the fodder
something withdrawn is pulled back, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: a run of letters from the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A prayer that has been taken back somehow shows faith or trust.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidence is something told privately, a secret shared in trust.

clue.text: …e.g., is in favor of former liberal"

blocks.note: to be for something is to be in favor of it
ex- means former
liberal in the sense of generous or plentiful

explanation.surface: Finishing the quote from 8 Down: Bush, for one, supports an ex-liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks political after Bush, but it means plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation e.g. stands for the Latin exempli gratia, which is read out in English as this phrase.

clue.text: Otherworldly extraterrestrial lines firs in nankeen caps…

indicators.note: a cap sits on top, so each word gives up only its head

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: An alien draws strange lines of fir trees on nankeen cloth, a fragment of a longer sentence running into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth. The ellipsis joins this clue to 15 Across in the surface only; each clue works alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means like an elf, fairylike, and so belonging to a magical other world.

clue.text: …with assistant wrapping pines

indicators.note: a thing wrapping another goes around it on both sides

blocks.note: an aide is an assistant
to pine is to yearn or long

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the alien comes with a helper who wraps up pine trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pines' looks like trees after the firs of 14 Across, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside is a preposition meaning together with or beside, so it can replace with.

clue.text: Passionate about hopin' to be heard with understanding

indicators.note: to be heard means spoken out loud, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: passionate about something is into it, and hopin' in the same dropped-g style is wishin'

explanation.surface: An enthusiast hoping to be listened to with sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g in hopin' tells you to drop it from the synonym too, so the sound ends in -shun.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is understanding reached instinctively, without conscious reasoning.

clue.text: Individual to hold this when talking!

definitions.text: Individual to hold this when talking!

blocks.note: surface reading: a lone person is asked to keep hold of something while speaking, like a talking stick
setter's reading: a personal device that one holds to the ear during a conversation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Individual' suggests a person, but it is the personal, one-each nature of the device; it also hints at a cell as the single unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile telephone is carried by each person and held up to speak through, the device the clue describes.

clue.text: Ape swallows an awning

indicators.note: whatever swallows something takes it inside itself

blocks.note: to ape is to copy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monkey gulps down a shop's sunshade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' is a verb here, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is a cloth covering hung above something for shade or shelter, as an awning is.

clue.text: Agenda in support of the metric system?

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
the gram is a basic unit of the metric system, an example signalled by the question mark

explanation.surface: A campaigner's manifesto backing metric measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: A program is a planned schedule of events or proposals, which an agenda also lists.

clue.text: Lecher is strangely artsy

indicators.note: done strangely means done in an odd way, so the letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A womaniser turns out, oddly, to be an arty type.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr, from the goat-like woodland gods of Greek myth, is a man with excessive sexual appetite.

clue.text: Eat properly inside and get bigger

indicators.note: inside means one word sits within the other

blocks.note: to sup is to eat supper
well means properly, as in done well

explanation.surface: Advice that eating right means growing up big.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell up is to expand or become enlarged, as a bruise does.

clue.text: Traitor is about to be in French surrender

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it

blocks.note: a rat is someone who betrays their side
être is the French verb to be

explanation.surface: A turncoat is ready to give up in France, a dig at French military history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In French' is not a container signal; it says which language translates 'to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a withdrawal or giving way in the face of opposition, close to a surrender.

clue.text: Right-winger bamboozled no one, capturing leadership of committee

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front
bamboozled means confused, so these letters are muddled up
something capturing another holds it within itself

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of committee

explanation.surface: A conservative politician fooled nobody yet still took over the running of a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A neocon, short for neoconservative, holds hawkish views on the political right.

clue.text: Fluid ounce, just when called for

indicators.note: something fluid flows and has no fixed shape, so its letters take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bartender pours a fluid ounce exactly when the recipe says to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid ounce' reads as a single measure; 'Fluid' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor comes in on cue at the signal, so the phrase means at exactly the right moment.

clue.text: One of the experts in a glazier's catalog?

blocks.note: a glazier fits panes of glass
a catalog is a list

explanation.surface: A specialist is named in a window-fitter's brochure.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the glazier's catalog is read as a list of panes.
explanation.definitionFit: A panelist sits on a panel, such as a group of experts answering questions on a show.

clue.text: Pope's irrational onus?

blocks.note: pi is the best-known irrational number
read as two words, on us: the rest sits on top of us in a down light

explanation.surface: A burden the poet Alexander Pope considered unreasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' suggests the poet; the question mark warns that 'onus' must be split.
explanation.definitionFit: Pius is the name taken by twelve popes, so it is a papal name rather than a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Someone who might be anxious to go over backward

indicators.note: going backward means the letters are taken from last to first

blocks.note: to recap is to go over the main points again

explanation.surface: A worrier is scared of toppling over backward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go over backward' reads as falling, but 'go over' is the wordplay and 'backward' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A worried person paces up and down, so a pacer is someone who might be nervous.

clue.text: Depraved ump is evil and unthinking

indicators.note: depraved means corrupted, so these letters are corrupted into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A baseball fan's rant: the corrupt umpire is wicked and brainless.
explanation.walkthrough: An ump is an umpire, the official in baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: Impulsive means acting on sudden urge without forethought, which is to say rashly.

clue.text: I need time to consider this simpleton's letters — some of them more than once

definitions.text: I need time to consider this

blocks.clueFragment: I need time to consider this
blocks.note: a plain request for time to think a decision over

blocks.clueFragment: simpleton's letters — some of them more than once
blocks.note: setter's reading: every letter of the phrase comes from the word simpleton, with some letters used repeatedly

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is not an anagram, since letters repeat; it is a check that the phrase uses only S, I, M, P, L, E, T, O and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom said when deferring a decision until after a night's rest, asking for time to think.
